name: Rara Lake
summary: Nepal's largest lake (also called Mahendra Tal), covering 10.8 sq km at 2,990m within Rara National Park in the remote far-northwest. Known for water that shifts color through the day (turquoise, midnight blue, orange-red at sunset) and for being one of the quietest, least-visited natural attractions in Nepal despite its scale. The national park hosts over 214 bird species and mammals including musk deer, Himalayan black bear, red panda, and snow leopard.

best_time_to_visit.primary: March to May (spring) and September to November (autumn)
best_time_to_visit.notes: Spring offers clear weather and melting-ice greenery. Autumn brings the clearest mountain views and moderate temperatures. Winter can bring heavy snowfall and very cold conditions; monsoon (June-August) brings rain and slippery trails.

route_from_kathmandu.distance_km: approx 370 km northwest of Kathmandu (as the crow flies); actual travel is longer via Nepalgunj
transport_options: Fastest: fly Kathmandu to Nepalgunj (~1 hour), then Nepalgunj to Talcha airport near Rara (~35-40 min), then 2-4 hour hike from Talcha to the lake
Overland/budget route: Kathmandu to Surkhet by bus/jeep (13-15 hours), then Surkhet to Jumla via rugged roads (8-10 hours), then trek from Jumla to Rara (approx 50km, 3 days)

difficulty_notes: Stays below 4,000m, making it more accessible than high-altitude treks in Everest or Annapurna regions, suitable for beginners in good health. Main challenges are remoteness and limited infrastructure rather than altitude.
time_required: 10-15 days round trip from Kathmandu depending on route chosen; shorter with the fly-in option
permits_required: TIMS card (NPR 2,000 / approx USD 15 for foreigners, NPR 1,000 / approx USD 8 for SAARC nationals - domestic Nepali citizens should confirm current requirement with NTB)
estimated_cost_usd: approx 950+ for a 15-day guided trek package (varies by operator and route)
